QF.id: Duplicate Share Certificates and Transmission of Securities_3

question.text: In the case of transmission of securities upon death of a single holder who had registered a nomination, which of the following is NOT required from the nominee?

answer.text: Certified death certificate of the deceased holder
Self-attested PAN card copy of the nominee
Succession certificate or probate of will

explanation.text: The Logic: Where a single holder has a registered nomination, the documents listed for the nominee in the workbook are the death certificate of the deceased holder, the duly filled transmission request form, and the self-attested PAN. Succession certificate, probate of will or letter of administration are listed in the no-nomination legal-heir process, not in the nominee process. The Trap: The succession certificate/probate is a standard transmission document in the absence of nomination, which is why it can appear correct here. For a nominee with a valid nomination, however, the workbook does not require it. Note: The single-holder-with-nomination nominee documents and the contrasting no-nomination legal-heir documents are set out on pages 156-157 of the NISM-Series-II-A Registrars and Transfer Agents (Corporate) Certification Examination workbook (October 2025).
